key_claims: Exercise may support the brain's glymphatic system, which clears waste during sleep.

Exercise can improve several processes involved in glymphatic function, including reducing blood pressure and vascular stiffness, improving neuron activation, reducing brain inflammation, lowering resting norepinephrine, and improving sleep.
Exercise may increase the quality of deep sleep and enhance slow wave activity associated with brain waste clearance.
The glymphatic system's role becomes increasingly important with age.
More than 10 million people worldwide are diagnosed with dementia each year, and there is currently no cure.
limitations: More research is needed to determine the most effective amount and type of exercise.
It is unclear if recommendations should change for people with cognitive decline or brain disease.
The review is based on existing studies in animals and humans, but specific details are not provided.
The exact mechanisms linking exercise to glymphatic function are not fully understood.
what_not_to_say: Exercise prevents or cures dementia or Alzheimer's disease.
Exercise directly clears waste from the brain.
A specific exercise type or duration is proven to benefit brain health.
Exercise is more effective than sleep for brain waste clearance.
